questions.q: What does the line `#!/bin/bash` at the top of a script do?
options: It's a comment describing the script's purpose
It tells the kernel which interpreter should run the rest of the file
It makes the file executable automatically
It sets the script's exit status to 0
questions.explain: The shebang line tells the kernel to hand the file to /bin/bash for interpretation, which is why Bash-specific syntax works correctly.

questions.q: You run `chmod +x deploy.sh` and then type `deploy.sh` with no path. What happens?
options: It runs normally, since chmod +x makes it runnable from anywhere
It likely fails with 'command not found', because the current directory usually isn't on PATH
It runs but ignores the shebang line
chmod +x has no effect on whether a script can run
questions.explain: Making a file executable doesn't put its directory on PATH. Without a leading ./ or a full path, the shell won't find a script in the current directory unless that directory is on PATH.

questions.q: After running a script, `echo $?` prints `0`. What does that mean?
options: The script produced no output
The script's most recent command (or an explicit exit) finished successfully
The script is still running
The script took 0 seconds to run
questions.explain: $? holds the exit status of the last command. By convention, 0 means success and any nonzero value signals some kind of failure.

questions.q: In the script `#!/bin/bash\n# backup.sh\necho hello`, what does the second line do?
options: Nothing — it's a comment, ignored by Bash
It sets a variable named backup.sh
It causes a syntax error, since only line one can start with #
It prints 'backup.sh' to the screen
questions.explain: Any line starting with # (other than the shebang on line one) is a comment. Bash skips it entirely — it exists only for human readers.

questions.q: A script ends with `exit 1`. What does that tell a program or cron job that calls it?
options: The script ran for 1 second
The script explicitly signaled failure, since the exit status is nonzero
The script succeeded, because 1 is a valid positive result
The script will automatically retry once
questions.explain: exit N sets the script's exit status to N. A nonzero status is the standard way a script signals failure to whatever called it.
